newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Eastern seen raising US$200 mln.
newsitem.headline: China Eastern seen raising US$200 mln.

text.p: China Eastern Airlines is expected to price its H-share at a price to earnings ratio of 9.6 to 10.5 times, raising about US$200 million, market sources said on Wednesday.
China Eastern is seeking a dual listing in Hong Kong and New York floating about 35 percent of the airline's enlarged share capital to the markets, they added.
Its flotation is expected to kick off later in January and Morgan Stanley is expected to be the global coordinator of the issue, sources said.
No further listing details are yet known, they added.

China Eastern operated a fleet of about 67 aircrafts, flying a total of 120 routes, comprising 15 international, 12 Hong Kong regional and 93 Hong Kong domestic at the end of 1996, Morgan Stanley said in a recent research report.
About 38 percent of the airline's sales revenue in 1995 was from domestic services while regional and international flight services contribute about 31 percent each, the report said.

China Eastern Airlines' posted a net profit of 633.8 million yuan in 1995, up 4.4 percent from 607.2 million a year earlier, it said. Turnover also rose 13.4 percent to 6.62 billion yuan in 1995, it said.
Morgan Stanley forecast the airline's net profit to fall by 13.4 percent in 1996 to 548.7 million yuan before moving up by 10.3 percent in 1997 to 604.9 million.
Analysts expected the issue to be welcomed by the market due to the recent demand for China related stock such as H-shares and red-chips.
